subsystems.name: Power system
subsystems.role: generates electricity at Jupiter, where sunlight is only about 4% as strong as at Earth.
parts: two five-panel solar arrays, more than 30 m tip to tip when deployed
batteries for eclipse and peak loads

subsystems.name: Radiation vault and avionics
subsystems.role: keeps the spacecraft's brain alive through repeated passes through Jupiter's radiation belts.
parts: avionics for pointing and instrument control

subsystems.name: Science payload
subsystems.role: nine instruments that together judge whether Europa's ocean could support life.
parts: MASPEX and SUDA for sampling gas and dust
ECM magnetometer and PIMS plasma instrument

subsystems.name: REASON radar booms
subsystems.role: ice-penetrating radar that sounds the shell and looks for the ocean below it.
parts: two long folded antennas, about 17.6 m each

subsystems.name: Propulsion and thermal control
subsystems.role: flies the gravity-assist trajectory, inserts into Jupiter orbit and keeps fuel and instruments at working temperature.

subsystems.name: Communications and navigation
subsystems.role: points the antenna at Earth and knows where it is in deep space.

buildSteps.title: Design the mission around flybys, not orbit
buildSteps.detail: Engineers choose to orbit Jupiter and dive past Europa roughly 49 times, so the spacecraft spends as little time as possible inside the worst radiation.

buildSteps.title: Build the spacecraft body
buildSteps.detail: The bus, vault and structural frame are assembled and its electronics tested before anything delicate goes in.

buildSteps.title: Make and fold the solar arrays
buildSteps.detail: Large panels of radiation-tolerant solar cells are built and then folded tight against the body for launch; at Jupiter they will yield only a few hundred watts.

buildSteps.title: Fit the radar antennas
buildSteps.detail: The two long REASON booms are stowed in their launch configuration, since they cannot be repaired or unfolded by hand once in space.

buildSteps.title: Integrate and test
buildSteps.detail: Instruments are mounted, then the whole spacecraft goes through vibration, thermal-vacuum and electromagnetic testing to prove it can survive launch and the cold of cruise.

buildSteps.title: Launch
buildSteps.detail: A Falcon Heavy lifted off from Kennedy Space Center on 14 October 2024, throwing the roughly 6,000 kg spacecraft onto a trajectory that will swing past Mars in March 2025 and Earth in December 2026.

buildSteps.title: Cruise and check out
buildSteps.detail: Over five and a half years the team flies the spacecraft, keeps its propellant lines and instruments warm, and rehearses the flyby sequences.

buildSteps.title: Arrive and fly by
buildSteps.detail: Jupiter orbit insertion in April 2030 begins a four-year prime mission of close passes — some as low as 25 km above the ice — returning radar, magnetic, spectral and dust data.

prerequisites.tech: Solar power in the outer solar system
prerequisites.why: Jupiter is far too dim for older missions, but modern solar arrays made solar-powered Jupiter exploration practical.
the spacecraft is large and heavy, and needs to reach Jupiter without a nuclear power source.
Jupiter's belts would destroy ordinary computers within hours of the planned flybys.
data comes back as a faint radio signal over hundreds of millions of kilometres.
sounding radar flown at Mars and used on Earth's ice sheets shows the technique works, though Europa's shell is a harder target.
detecting organic molecules at very low concentrations has been done at Saturn and comets, but the sensitivity needed to detect life-related chemistry is at the edge of what has flown.

pathway.milestone: cruise phase with gravity assists from Mars (2025) and Earth (2026)
pathway.unlocks: a low-cost way to reach Jupiter without a massive launch vehicle.

pathway.milestone: Jupiter orbit insertion and the first Europa flybys
pathway.unlocks: close-up radar, magnetic and imaging data from a moon never seen at this resolution.

pathway.milestone: roughly 49 flybys measuring ice-shell thickness, ocean salinity and surface chemistry
pathway.unlocks: a defensible answer on whether Europa's ocean is habitable.

pathway.milestone: results feeding a possible Europa lander and other ocean-world missions
pathway.unlocks: the step from assessing habitability to directly sampling the ice and, eventually, searching for life itself.
